cues.zh: 就是它们不一定是规整的正方形或长方形
cues.en: is that since they are not necessarily perfect square or rectangles

cues.zh: 可用空间的大小取决于地块形状。
cues.en: the amount of usable space depends on the shape.

cues.zh: 这样一来，75平方米的地块实际可用性可能和60平方米的差不多
cues.en: In that way, a 75 square metre lot may be as practically useful as a 60 square metre one

cues.zh: 你会看到很多大小不一的地块紧挨在一起，价格却相同。
cues.en: and you'll see lots of dissimilar sizes right next to each other priced the same.

cues.zh: 《金融时报》探讨了为什么
cues.en: The Financial Times talks about why

cues.zh: 东京是住宅建设不断增加、但房价不涨的地方。
cues.en: Tokyo is the land of rising home construction but not prices.

cues.zh: Takahiko Noguchi，规划部门负责人
cues.en: Takahiko Noguchi, head of planning

cues.zh: 港区规划科的这位负责人解释了原因。
cues.en: section in Minato Ward explains why.

cues.zh: “拆除建筑没有法律限制，”他说。
cues.en: "There is no legal restraint on demolishing a building,” he says.

cues.zh: “人们有权使用自己的土地，所以基本上邻居无权阻止开发。”
cues.en: “People have the right to use their land so basically neighbouring people have no right to stop development.”

cues.zh: 对，所以只要你遵守分区法规，就可以放心建造。
cues.en: Right, so provided you follow zoning regulations, you're A-OK to build.

cues.zh: 哇，哇，哇！这80年代的音乐是怎么回事。我自己也正这么想。
cues.en: Woah, woah, woah! What's with the 80's music. I was thinking the same thing myself.

cues.zh: 我是说，我出生在80年代，也许是我的潜意识想把我带回那个时代
cues.en: I mean, I was born in the 80's, maybe it's my subconscious trying to bring me back to a time

cues.zh: 那个我父亲二十多岁时就能买得起新房的时代
cues.en: a time where my father in his 20's could afford a new home

cues.zh: 仅靠他一个人的工资就能养活全家。啊，美好的旧时光！
cues.en: and support the entire family on his wage alone. Ah, the good old days!

cues.zh: 但回到正题。我相信你一定在想
cues.en: But back on topic. I'm sure you must be wondering

cues.zh: 东京或日本真的是一个宜居的地方吗？
cues.en: Is Tokyo or Japan really a good place to live?

cues.zh: 也许你在想
cues.en: And maybe you're thinking

cues.zh: 你展示的房子连院子都没有，而且又小又挤，不是吗？
cues.en: The houses you showed didn't even have yards and aren't they small and cramped?

cues.zh: 另外，你可能听说过，在日本，房子只能撑30年，还有大量废弃建筑！
cues.en: Also, you may have heard that in Japan, homes only last 30 years and there are tons of abandoned buildings!

cues.zh: 是啊是啊，我懂你的意思。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah, I hear ya.

cues.zh: 我正在做视频聊这些话题
cues.en: I'm making videos that talk about those topics

cues.zh: 还会有一些新的看房视频给你们，稍等一下。
cues.en: and also have some new home tours to show you, hang tight.

cues.zh: 与此同时，欢迎在评论区提问。
cues.en: In the meantime, feel free to ask some questions in the comments section.

cues.zh: 趁我还没忘，我要感谢所有通过Patreon支持这些迷你纪录片的人。
cues.en: And before I forget, I want to give a shout out to all those who support these mini-docs through Patreon.

cues.zh: 非常感谢！
cues.en: Thank you so much!

cues.zh: 一如既往，感谢观看，我们下期见。
cues.en: As always, thanks for watching and will catch you on the flipside.
